pageSummary:
Client background
Studio Arts College International (SACI) is a U.S.‑accredited art school in Florence, Italy. It was founded in 1975 by Fulbright scholar and painter Jules Maidoff and is the oldest American art school in Florence. SACI holds the distinction of being the first art school in Europe accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD). Over several decades SACI has welcomed thousands of students pursuing degrees or study abroad experiences in studio art, design, conservation and art history. Students study in two historical palazzi—Palazzo dei Cartelloni and Palazzo Maidoff—located in Florence's historic center Palazzo dei Cartelloni is a 17th‑century Renaissance palace built for mathematician Vincenzo Viviani, a pupil of Galileo Galilei; its façade describes Galileo's discoveries and the interior features painted ceilings and frescoed walls. Palazzo Maidoff is two blocks from the Duomo and offers studio spaces around a courtyard. Studying in these landmark buildings underscores SACI's prestige and connection to the Renaissance tradition.

Project overview
Objective. SACI's communications team and Stoltze Design partnered to redesign SACI's website and digital identity. The goal was to simplify and streamline SACI's extensive information, modernize its visual identity, and create a responsive, user‑friendly site that showcases programs, admissions, student life, events and galleries. The redesign was part of a broader rebranding effort; Stoltze introduced a new logo that blended traditional proportions with bold color and graceful typography to reflect SACI's commitment to excellence and accessibility.

Initial state & challenges. Prior to redesign, SACI maintained a complex platform containing years of content. Stakeholders reported that information architecture, navigation, and page layouts made it difficult for prospective students to discover programs or apply. Christina Gednalske, who led ongoing content management, explains that the Drupal redesign involved large‑scale content migration and responsive design, creating robust directories, forms, unique page templates and an extensive sitemap covering students, admissions, courses, events, galleries, faculty, blog pieces and alumni. Even after launch, continual additions and updates were needed to address feedback from board members, faculty, staff, prospective and admitted students, and alumni. The communications team sought to maintain user friendliness while adapting to these changes.

Scope. Working remotely from Florence with Stoltze Design in Boston, the team established goals for the redesign: simplify and streamline the vast content, update the UI, create a responsive experience across desktop, mobile and tablet, make learning about programs easy and enticing, and improve and simplify the application and admissions process. Additionally, the site needed to capture the atmosphere of Florence while conveying credibility comparable to top U.S. art and design schools.

Design solution and implementation

Extensive sitemap & user flows: The team designed a comprehensive sitemap based on typical user journeys for prospective and admitted students, parents, study‑abroad advisors, alumni, faculty and board members. Iterative sitemapping and user flows considered research and application steps, academic information needs, student life queries and alumni engagement. Drupal's flexible taxonomy system was used to organize content by degree type, term, course category, faculty type and other vocabularies.

Content types & templates: The project created tailored content types such as Programs, Courses, Classes, Faculty/Alumni, Events & Exhibitions, Blog (News) and Student Gallery. Each content type included custom fields (e.g., term, degree type, category) and standardized templates for list and detail views. For example, Program pages display degree type headers, descriptions and a grid of programs driven by taxonomy. Course pages include filters by term and category and dynamically list classes. Events lists use date fields to show upcoming events and an event carousel on the home page.

User roles & permissions: The site defined roles for administrators, editors and faculty, with Drupal's revision and publishing controls enabled by default. This allowed controlled content updates while ensuring that only published content is visible to visitors.

Visual design & user experience
New identity: Stoltze Design created a new logo and brand system that merges traditional proportion with contemporary typography and bold color, mirroring SACI's blend of Renaissance tradition and modern accessibility.

Full‑page scroll & responsive layout: The home page uses a full‑page scroll to present sections such as hero media, promoted programs, news grid and event carousel. A custom script transforms the header into a fixed "mini‑header" on scroll. Responsive design ensures that the site functions seamlessly on desktops, tablets and mobile devices.

Hero media & storytelling: Administrators can choose a hero image or embedded video (YouTube or Vimeo) for the home page; the video field overrides the image when present. WYSIWYG fields allow for customizable taglines such as "College of Art…" and "Florence, Italy". These elements give visitors an immediate sense of SACI's location and mission.

Promoted items & dynamic carousels: A promoted items field collection lets administrators spotlight programs with an image, category, title, description and call‑to‑action button. The home page also contains a news grid showing the five most recent blog posts and an event carousel that displays upcoming events marked "promoted to home page". Pagination and text blocks provide additional context and link to full articles or events.

Navigation & global elements: The site features a top navigation linking to Alumni, Request Information and Apply pages; a main navigation listing primary sections like About and Academics; and a footer with links back to the home page, contact blocks, social media links and WYSIWYG areas for facility hours and contact information. Drupal's search module provides site‑wide search.

Accessibility & usability: Custom block placements allow administrators to insert calls‑to‑action (e.g., "Take the next steps…" banner) within specific regions. The site integrates Chosen for enhanced select boxes, Google Analytics for tracking, Metatag for SEO, and ShareThis for social sharing. The domain is configured to redirect all variants, ensuring consistency and security.

Technology stack
CMS: The entire site runs on Drupal, selected for its flexible content model, taxonomy system and robust module ecosystem. Custom content types, fields and views were built to accommodate SACI's complex information architecture.

Front‑end: Responsive layouts were built using HTML5/CSS and JavaScript. The full‑page scroll effect and header transformation rely on custom JS. The design follows the brand guidelines established by Stoltze, ensuring consistency across devices.

Third‑party services: Video hosting uses YouTube and Vimeo. Social sharing is handled via ShareThis, and analytics through Google Analytics. SEO metadata is controlled via the Metatag module.

Impact and results
After launch, SACI and Stoltze reported measurable improvements:

Enhanced accessibility and user experience. Stoltze notes that the redesigned website improved accessibility for applicants and administrative staff and provided a streamlined application process. Flexible content components made it easier for staff to update pages and showcase student stories and events.

Increased engagement and enrollment. SACI reported a boost in enrollment following the site's launch. The new design and improved application workflows likely contributed to higher conversion rates.

Ongoing adaptability. Continuous updates to information architecture, UX writing, content and page layouts have maintained the site's relevance as SACI's programs evolve. The flexible Drupal framework and modular design support these iterations without major overhauls.

Conclusion
The collaboration between Studio Arts College International, Stoltze Design and the Knectar development team yielded a comprehensive redesign of SACI's digital presence. Grounded in the institution's rich history and prestige, the project delivered a modern, responsive website that simplifies complex information, enhances the user journey and reflects SACI's blend of Renaissance heritage and contemporary art education. By leveraging Drupal's flexible CMS, thoughtful information architecture, dynamic storytelling components and a refreshed visual identity, the new site not only improved internal workflows but also increased prospective student engagement and enrollment. The project demonstrates how strategic design and content management can revitalize an educational institution's online identity while honoring its historical roots.
